name: Centro and Barrio Antiguo
description: The historic core around the Macroplaza and the Santa Lucia riverwalk, with Barrio Antiguo's low colonial houses turned into bars, galleries and small cafes. It is the one part of Monterrey where you can genuinely live on foot, with the metro, museums and cheap taquerias all within a few blocks.
bestFor: Nomads who want to skip the car and walk to cafes, metro and nightlife.
pros: Walkable with two metro lines through it
Cheap street food and old-school cantinas
Museums and the Santa Lucia riverwalk on the doorstep
cons: Barrio Antiguo gets very loud on weekend nights
Quiet, emptier blocks feel sketchy after dark
Older buildings with weak air conditioning in a brutal summer

name: San Pedro Garza Garcia
tagline: Mexico's wealthiest suburb, under the mountain
description: A separate municipality southwest of the city, sitting below the Sierra Madre and holding Del Valle's towers, the Calzada and Fashion Drive malls, and most of Monterrey's corporate offices. Streets are clean, safe and heavily landscaped, with the best restaurants and gyms in northern Mexico.
bestFor: Nomads with a strong budget who want the safest streets and the best amenities.
pros: Safest area in the metro region by a wide margin
Top restaurants, gyms, coworking and clinics
Chipinque hiking trails right behind it
cons: Built for cars, hard to live here without one
Feels sanitised and disconnected from real Monterrey

name: Valle Oriente
tagline: Glass towers, malls and new apartments
description: A modern high-rise district on the eastern edge of San Pedro, built around Paseo San Pedro and Punto Valle malls, corporate towers and a wall of new apartment buildings. Almost everything here was built in the last twenty years, so flats come with gyms, pools, coworking lounges and solid fibre.
bestFor: Nomads who want a new-build apartment with a gym and fast internet, no fuss.
pros: Newest apartment stock with strong amenities
Malls, supermarkets and cinemas within walking distance
cons: Expensive, close to San Pedro pricing
Heavy traffic on Lazaro Cardenas at rush hour

name: Obispado
tagline: Older middle-class streets on the hill
description: A central hillside neighbourhood around the colonial Obispado museum, with 1950s and 1960s houses, mature trees and views over the city. It sits between Centro and San Pedro, so both are ten minutes away, and rents are far below either. Small cafes and neighbourhood taquerias line Padre Mier.
bestFor: Nomads who want a central location and a real neighbourhood on a moderate budget.
pros: Central position between Centro and San Pedro
Much cheaper than Valle Oriente for similar space
Leafy streets with genuine local character
cons: Steep hills make walking hard in summer heat
Housing stock is older, air conditioning varies
Thin nightlife, you head to Centro or San Pedro

name: Tecnologico
tagline: Student blocks around the Tec campus
description: The area surrounding the Tecnologico de Monterrey campus in the south of the city, full of shared houses, cheap rentals, taco stands, print shops and student bars. Distrito Tec redevelopment has added cafes and bike lanes. The cheapest way to live centrally, if you can live with student energy.
bestFor: Budget nomads who want low rent, cheap food and easy people to meet.
pros: Lowest rents of any central area
Tacos and set lunches for $3 to $5
Young crowd and easy to make friends
cons: Noisy during term, dead over holidays
Surrounding blocks are rough in places
Very few flats aimed at professionals
